papers.title: TelecomGPT: A Framework to Build Telecom-Specific Large Language Models
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Machine Learning in Communications and Networking (TMLCN)
papers.base_model: General-purpose instruction-tuned LLM; specific checkpoint NOT named in retrieved text. Paper is deliberately framework-agnostic ('adapt any general purpose LLM')
papers.method: Three stages: continual pre-training (causal LM) -> instruction tuning (SFT) -> alignment tuning via DPO
papers.dataset_name: OpenTelecom (pre-training), TelecomInstruct (instruction), TelecomAlign (DPO preference)
papers.dataset_size: OpenTelecom: 1679.5M training tokens + 16.89M validation tokens (3GPP std 193M, IEEE std 7.5M, arXiv 893M, books 1.9M, patents 253.2M, StackExchange 51.9M, Wikipedia 18.9M, GitHub code 260.1M). Instruction/preference set sizes not reported in samples.

papers.title: Tele-LLMs: A Series of Specialized Large Language Models for Telecommunications
papers.base_model: TinyLlama-1.1B, Phi-1.5B, Gemma-2B, Gemma-2-2B, LLaMA-3.2-1B, LLaMA-3.2-3B, LLaMA-3-8B
papers.method: Continual pre-training with FULL fine-tuning. PEFT/LoRA tested and REJECTED: LoRA r=64, alpha=32, dropout=0.1 - 'for smaller models LoRA can initially inject telecom knowledge but quickly saturates due to its limited capacity'; on LLaMA-3-8B 'the gradient norm of the LoRA method remained extremely low'. Full FT settings: AdamW, weight decay 0.1, max grad norm 1, cosine schedule to 10% of max LR, 10%-of-epoch linear warmup, batch 4M tokens, seq len 8192, max LR 1e-5 (LLaMA) / 2e-5 (Gemma), mixed precision + sample packing + block attention, 2 epochs, 5% SlimPajama mixed in. Instruction-tuning stage: Q-LoRA, 8-bit init, rank 8, on Q/K/V/O, batch 8, grad-accum 2, LR 2e-4, AdamW, lora_alpha 32, dropout 0.05.
papers.dataset_name: Tele-Data (corpus) + Tele-Eval (evaluation)
papers.dataset_size: Tele-Data: arXiv 90k papers/4GB/1.08B tokens; 3GPP standards 2.8k docs/334MB/86.45M tokens; Wikipedia 19.5k articles/123MB/26.44M tokens; Web 740k links/6.8GB/1.55B tokens. Tele-Eval: 750k open-ended Q&A pairs (1% retention after filtering).
papers.training_time: ~5000 GPU hours total for the released series
papers.inference_latency: Evaluation-side: Mixtral-8x-7B LLM-judge took ~50 ms per question on a single NVIDIA A6000
papers.main_results: Average relative improvement of 25% on Tele-Eval (LLM-Eval metric). LLM-Eval: Gemma-2B 13.59 -> Gemma-2B-Tele 17.07; Phi-1.5 14.87 -> Phi-1.5-Tele 13.06 (degraded) -> Phi-1.5-Tele-Alpaca 18.84; Gemma-2B-Tele-Alpaca 25.31; Gemma-2B-it 19.84 -> 24.83. Gemma-2B-Standards UNDERPERFORMED base on overall Tele-Eval (11.18 vs 13.59). LLaMA-3-8B-Tele +10% on GSM-8K.
baselines: Original un-adapted models (Gemma-2B, Phi-1.5, LLaMA-3-8B, TinyLlama)
papers.main_limitation: Task is telecom knowledge/literature (Q&A, citation prediction and recommendation), NOT network management decisions or network KPIs. No compression experiments. Full FT costs 8xA6000 and 5000 GPU hours.

papers.title: Harnessing the Power of LLMs, Informers and Decision Transformers for Intent-driven RAN Management in 6G
papers.base_model: LLaMA (used as the baseline in Fig. 6). EXACT VARIANT AND PARAMETER COUNT NOT REPORTED. The '10-billion parameter model' mentioned is a generic memory illustration, not the actual model.
papers.method: QLoRA (all four components: 4-bit NormalFloat quantisation, double quantisation, paged optimisation, LoRA) + RAG module
papers.dataset_name: Custom dataset built from network simulations, in three segments: query-response pairs, intent type+magnitude labels, RAG corpus
papers.dataset_size: not reported ('hundreds or even thousands of query-response pairs can be generated')

HDTGA orchestration vs baselines: throughput +19.3% (abstract) / +19.4% (body), delay -48.5%, energy efficiency +54.9%. NOTE: the body text reverses the delay/energy-efficiency percentages relative to the abstract - an internal inconsistency in the paper.

papers.main_limitation: No base-model identification, no hardware, no dataset size, no latency - not reproducible as published. Simulation-based, not a live network. Preprint.

papers.title: Leveraging Multi-Agent System (MAS) and Fine-Tuned Small Language Models (SLMs) for Automated Telecom Network Troubleshooting
papers.base_model: Unsloth/DeepSeek-R1-Qwen-3-8B (8B, reasoning); also Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-1.7B for the size comparison. Orchestration LLM: GPT-4o mini
papers.method: Two-stage: SFT (LoRA warm-up on labelled QA pairs) then RFT with LoRA + GRPO, in the TRL library with ZeRO Stage-2 DeepSpeed. Rewards: format rewards (regex/XML tags) + RAGAS-based rewards (completeness, relevancy, groundedness).
papers.dataset_name: Proprietary telecom troubleshooting documents (RAN power-system faults; Core PDU-session degradation) indexed into a HippoRAG knowledge graph
papers.dataset_size: not given here; the companion paper (arXiv:2509.25736 / arXiv:2607.02523) reports 50 SME-validated seed pairs + 500 synthetically generated RFT pairs
papers.gpu_hardware: 7 x NVIDIA RTX A6000 (48 GB VRAM each). Allocation: 1 GPU vLLM Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B; 1 GPU vLLM Qwen3-8B (RAGAS judge, thinking disabled); 2 GPUs TRL-vLLM DeepSeek-R1-Qwen-3-8B.
papers.training_time: Entire training process completes within 3 days with uniform chunking; ~20 hours to resume from a checkpoint
papers.main_results: Mean troubleshooting time reduced ~6x per node vs human engineers; accuracy improved 10% vs human-driven process. RFT for the 8B model: RAGAS reward 3.44 -> 5.19; Format reward 2.52 -> 5.31; Total reward 5.96 -> 10.51; reward std-dev 2.17 -> 0.38. Size scaling: 8B reaches peak reward ~10; 4B and 1.7B 'show modest improvements but consistently lower rewards'. Fine-tuned 8B judged comparable in quality to GPT-4o-mini, while the base model produces only generic high-level answers.
papers.code_data_url: not found (proprietary documents; Hypha and HippoRAG are OSS)
papers.main_limitation: Proprietary dataset, no public code. Rewards are LLM/RAGAS-judged rather than ground-truth-labelled. The '6x faster / +10% accuracy' is vs human engineers, not vs an automated baseline. Preprint.

papers.title: Edge-Deployable LLM Fine-Tuning on a Single GPU for Telecom Network Troubleshooting
papers.base_model: unsloth/Qwen2.5-7B (7.61B params, 28 layers, 28 Q-heads / 4 KV-heads, GQA) and unsloth/DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B-unsloth-bnb-4bit (8.2B params, 36 layers, 32 Q / 8 KV heads). Cross-architecture validation with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. All support 131072-token context.
papers.method: LoRA restricted to q_proj, k_proj, v_proj; two-stage SFT -> RFT (GRPO/TRL); Unsloth framework with 4-bit quantisation, FlashAttention2, XFormers, KV-cache acceleration, torch.compile/inductor. Profiling sweep over max sequence length, GPU-memory utilisation, LoRA rank, generation count.
papers.dataset_name: Telecom troubleshooting dataset: QA pairs augmented with top-3 retrieved context documents
papers.dataset_size: 50 SME-validated seed pairs (SFT) + 500 synthetically generated RFT pairs; average token length of top-3 chunks ~16126 tokens
papers.gpu_hardware: 1 x NVIDIA RTX A6000, 48 GB VRAM (edge-class); cross-checked against a 4xGH200 cluster
papers.training_time: 250 steps: 1k input tokens = 116 min; 5k = 173 min; 10k = 229 min; 10k with 4 generations at 0.6 util = 313 min. Llama-3.1-8B: 250 steps at 20k input tokens in ~29 min (~7x faster than Qwen2.5-7B).
papers.inference_latency: '7-8B parameter models serve requests in seconds on the RTX A6000' - no millisecond figure reported
papers.vram_profile: At 50k seq-len / 0.7 GPU-util: compile 16.2 GB + KV cache 11.2 GB = 329k KV tokens. Sweep: 1k->438k tokens, 20k->415k, 40k->358k, 50k->329k; 60k and 80k fail with CAIM error; 50k/0.3 fails with Cache Error; 50k/0.8-0.9 -> 411k tokens.
papers.main_results: Safe operating envelope on 48 GB: 50k max sequence length at 0.7 GPU utilisation. Sequence length >=60k produced CUDA CannotAccessIllegalMemory errors on Qwen2.5-7B but NOT on Llama-3.1-8B (60k succeeded) - thresholds are not portable across model families. Batch size >=4 OOMs above 20k tokens on both. Input tokens >10k at 0.7 util OOMs at step 155/250. DeepSeek-R1 with hybrid tokenizer strategy achieved substantial gains in factual grounding and response consistency over Qwen2.5-7B.
papers.main_limitation: A profiling/characterisation study, not a quality study - reports memory/time envelopes and reward trajectories rather than network-decision accuracy. Preprint, 6 pages.

papers.title: LLM-Based Emulation of the Radio Resource Control Layer: Towards AI-Native RAN Protocols
papers.base_model: Llama-3 8B, Llama-3.1 8B, Llama-3.2 3B, Llama-3.2 1B
papers.method: SFT + LoRA (adapters on attention projections AND MLP layers, alpha=2r, dropout=0). LoRA ranks r in {4,8,16} benchmarked against full fine-tuning. bf16, AdamW, token-level cross-entropy. LR 2e-5 (full FT) / 3e-4 (LoRA, cosine decay, 100-step warmup). Quantisation: weight-only INT4 (Q4_K_M, GGUF). Prompting: NoSys / RRC / RRC_constrain (schema-bounded).
papers.dataset_name: Proprietary multi-vendor 4G/5G RRC traces, formulated as segmentation-safe QA pairs preserving ASN.1 via linearisation before BPE
papers.dataset_size: 30000 5G request-response pairs + 4800 QA turns from 4G/LTE sessions
papers.gpu_hardware: NR dataset: 2 x NVIDIA A100 80 GB (PCIe), 52-core CPU, 512 GB RAM; ~29 GB VRAM per inference thread (GGUF), ~110 GB across two cards for training. LTE dataset: 4 x NVIDIA GH200 nodes (Grace 72-core CPU + H100 96 GB HBM3), cluster of 1320 nodes, HPE Cray Slingshot-11; single-accelerator config = 1 x H100 (96 GB) inside one GH200.
papers.training_time: Converged in ~8.4k steps; deliberately truncated to avoid 'unnecessary GPU hours'
papers.inference_latency: Median latency to generate one DL RRC message (LTE, RRC_constrain): L-3 8B FP16 + LoRA-r16 = 3544 ms; L-3 8B Q4_K_M + LoRA-r16 = 2556 ms; L-3.1 8B FP16 = 3609 ms; L-3.1 8B Q4_K_M = 2581 ms; L-3.2 3B (full FT) FP16 = 2341 ms / Q4_K_M = 1733 ms; L-3.2 1B (full FT) FP16 = 2093 ms / Q4_K_M = 2025 ms. RRC (unconstrained): L-3 8B FP16 = 3418 ms vs Q4_K_M = 2519 ms. Edge vs datacentre with Llama-3.2-1B/INT4: Apple M2 Max 1.84 s vs 1xGH200(H100) 1.092 s; throughput 0.54 vs 0.92 req/s; energy ~7.7 mWh/message (M2, 15 W cap) vs ~0.200 Wh/message (GH200, 660 W cap).
papers.model_size_after_compression: INT4 Q4_K_M GGUF; ~29 GB VRAM per inference thread
papers.main_results: Median cosine similarity 0.97 for the 8B model = +61% relative over zero-shot. L-3 8B Q4_K_M RRC_constrain: ASN.1 pass median 1.000, similarity 0.992 median, SMC 0.993. Zero-shot baselines on NR dataset: Gemini 1.5-Flash 0.585, GPT-4o 0.496, Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 0.768, GPT-o3-mini 0.705, original Llama 3-8B 0.600, RRC-LLM (fine-tuned) 0.970. Quantisation-latency trade-off: INT4 consistently reduces median latency by ~20-30% vs FP16 with small average reductions in ASN.1/SMC pass (a few percentage points, backbone-dependent); largest drops on the smallest backbone (1B). LoRA rank ablation (best validation loss, LTE): on 8B backbones r=16 matches or slightly surpasses full FT; on 3B/1B full FT remains advantageous; best-two gap delta ~6e-4. L-3.2 1B SMC: FP16 0.989 -> Q4_K_M 0.883.
baselines: Zero-shot Gemini 1.5-Flash, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2, GPT-o3-mini, original Llama-3-8B
papers.code_data_url: not found (corpus is proprietary multi-vendor operator traces)
papers.main_limitation: Proprietary dataset, not reproducible. Latency in the 1-3.6 second range is far above real RRC control-plane budgets; sub-100 ms is explicitly framed as future work. Preprint.

papers.title: Toward Autonomous O-RAN: A Multi-Scale Agentic AI Framework for Real-Time Network Control and Management
papers.base_model: Nvidia Nemotron (LLM rApp, Non-RT); GPT-OSS (SLM xApp, Near-RT); Wireless Physical-layer Foundation Model (WPFM) dApp (RT)
papers.method: Deployment-scale separation, NOT compression. Different-sized models assigned to different control loops. LLM translates operator intent to A1 policy via an MCP tool interface; SLM performs PRB allocation via E2SM-RC; WPFM is fine-tuned on demand.
papers.dataset_name: Live 5G testbed based on srsRAN with four active slices; E2SM-KPM telemetry (5-second sliding window at Near-RT, 1-minute summaries at Non-RT). Plus two IEEE DataPort IQ datasets: vehicular technology recognition (LTE, 5G NR, Wi-Fi, ITS-G5, C-V2X) and LTE/NR interference.
papers.gpu_hardware: LLM: H200 GPU. SLM: RTX 5090 GPU. WPFM: Nvidia Jetson Xavier NX.
papers.training_time: WPFM fine-tuning: first epoch ~17 s reaching 58.92% (technology recognition) / 82.28% (interference detection); fully fine-tuned after ~340 s
papers.inference_latency: WPFM (RT, Xavier NX): 0.847 +/- 0.04 ms. SLM (Near-RT, RTX 5090): 793 +/- 3 ms. LLM (Non-RT, H200): 9364 +/- 59 ms.
papers.main_results: Agentic (SLM+LLM supervision) vs SLM-only: average VIP throughput +6% after promoting slice 4 to VIP, while preserving average 22 ms latency for the latency-sensitive slice; SLM-only alone reaches only 10.5 Mbps VIP throughput and trades away latency protection. Agentic beats static allocation and a heuristic controller on throughput, delay and resource efficiency. Table I explicitly frames the latency/cost ladder (Low/Medium/High) as scaling proportionally with control domain.
papers.code_data_url: not found for this paper; referenced WPFM and datasets are public (IEEE DataPort links given in the paper)
papers.main_limitation: Proof-of-concept on one live testbed; no fine-tuning hyperparameters, no model parameter counts, no training hardware for the SLM itself. The RT dApp API and RT RIC are not yet standardised in O-RAN, so the architecture is provisional. Preprint.

papers.title: NetIntent: Leveraging Large Language Models for End-to-End Intent-Based SDN Automation
papers.affiliation: King Fahd University of Petroleum & Minerals
papers.venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society (OJ-COMS)
papers.base_model: 33 open-source LLMs spanning 1.1B-70B, including TinyLlama:1.1b, Deepseek-coder:1.3b, Phi:2.7b, Starcoder:3b, Llama3.2:3b, Phi3:3.8b, Orca-mini:3b, Qwen:4b, Yi:6b, Codellama:7b, Llama2:7b, Llama3:8b, Llama3.1:8b, Qwen2.5:7b, Mistral:7b, Dolphin-Mistral:7b, Wizardlm2:7b, Codegemma:7b, Zephyr:7b, Qwen2:7b, Mistral-nemo:12b, Codestral:22b, Deepseek-coder-v2:16b, QwQ:32b, Gemma2-27b, Codellama:34b, Command-r:35b, Llama2:70b, Llama3.3:70b, Codellama:70b
papers.method: NO FINE-TUNING - in-context/few-shot learning with dynamic context-example selection (Max Marginal Relevance); temperature 0.6 / top-p 0.3 (translation) and 0.3 / 0.5 (conflict detection); served via Ollama
papers.dataset_name: IBNBench (new): Intent2Flow-ODL, Intent2Flow-ONOS, FlowConflict-ODL, FlowConflict-ONOS. Plus existing: Formal Specification, NFV Configuration.
papers.dataset_size: Intent2Flow-ODL 52 pairs; Intent2Flow-ONOS 50 pairs; FlowConflict-ODL 60 pairs (19 conflicting); FlowConflict-ONOS 74 pairs (27 conflicting); Formal Specification 1500 pairs; NFV Configuration 120 pairs. 50/50 context/test split.
papers.gpu_hardware: No training. Inference: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 5995WX (64-core), 500 GB RAM, 1 x NVIDIA RTX A6000 (48 GB VRAM)
papers.inference_latency: Runtime reported per model. Example: Codellama-34b required over 10 seconds per inference, whereas Qwen2.5-7B achieved competitive performance in under 2 seconds. 70B models could not be evaluated at larger context sizes due to hardware memory constraints.
papers.main_results: Formal Specification dataset: QwQ-fusion and Command-r (32-35B) >=99%; Codellama:7b and Mistral:7b up to 95% with lower latency; mid-sized models gained up to 20% accuracy from 0 to 9 context examples (Dolphin-Mistral:7b 0% -> 80%); TinyLlama:1.1b and Deepseek-coder:1.3b significantly lower accuracy. Intent2Flow-ONOS: Llama3.3:70b 88% zero-shot, surpassing Llama2:70b and Codellama:70b; Codestral:22b outperformed Command-r:35b. Conflict detection (FlowConflict-ONOS): QwQ:32b perfect (F1 1.0); Llama3.3:70b 94% accuracy, FPR 0.02, F1 0.78; Llama2:70b perfect recall but 52 false positives. Codellama:7b, Codegemma-7b, Dolphin-Mistral-7b, Deepseek-coder-1.3b exceeded 87% FPR. KEY CLAIM: 'larger model size does not inherently guarantee superior performance'.
baselines: All 33 LLMs serve as mutual baselines
papers.code_data_url: Yes - datasets and benchmarking results released (GitHub link referenced as [48]); NetIntent framework implementation released
papers.main_limitation: No fine-tuning, so it does not test whether a small fine-tuned model could replace a large prompted one. Results are highly prompt- and schema-sensitive, which the authors acknowledge.

papers.title: MERLOT: A Distilled LLM-based Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Scalable Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.note: arXiv v1 (Nov 2024) had 4 authors; the published version adds Xutong Li
papers.base_model: GPT-2-base (12 layers, hidden dim 768, ~117M parameters)
papers.method: Knowledge distillation (teacher-student, composite loss L = (1-alpha)*CE(student, hard label) + alpha*KL(student || teacher)) PLUS pruning of the MoE gating network ('a distilled, PRUNED GPT-2-base model') PLUS MoE with hard one-hot gating (exactly one expert active) PLUS architectural change (direct classification from the final decoder token instead of generative/prompt-based classification)
papers.dataset_name: 10 encrypted traffic datasets: APP-53 2023, CSIC 2010, CSTNET 2023, CW-100 2018, DAPT 2020, DoHBrw 2020, ISCX Botnet 2014, ISCX Tor 2016, ISCX VPN 2016, USTC TFC 2016
papers.dataset_size: ~527600 samples total: APP-53 109.8K/54 labels; CSIC 2010 34.5K/2; CSTNET 2023 97.6K/20; CW-100 2018 7.4K/100; DAPT 2020 10.0K/2; DoHBrw 2020 47.8K/2; ISCX Botnet 2014 25.0K/5; ISCX Tor 2016 40.0K/8; ISCX VPN 2016 64.8K/14; USTC TFC 2016 50.7K/20
papers.inference_latency: 'Consumes 85-90% less inference time and memory usage' than 7B TrafficLLM - no absolute ms value reported
papers.model_size_after_compression: MERLOT 500M / 660M / 1.25B parameters (the MoE aggregates multiple distilled experts, so it is NOT sub-117M)
papers.main_limitation: Loses on 2 of 10 datasets - compression is not uniformly lossless. No training hardware, no absolute latency, no compressed size in MB. Workshop paper, 5 pages.

papers.title: Pruned Traffic Trees: Native Semantic Compression with a Protocol-Structured Model Family for Encrypted Traffic Classification

papers.base_model: Not a pretrained LLM - a protocol-structured model family built on Protocol Tree Graphs (PTGs) with flow-level self-supervised learning. Parameter count reported only as relative reductions.
papers.method: Structured pruning at the PROTOCOL level: learned field salience + TopK + k closure selects which protocol fields and structural contexts to retain, producing 'Distilled PTGs' (PTG-Ds). Plus width reduction via structure-aligned transfer, plus flow-level logits distillation. Three levels: PTT-Full -> PTT-Distilled -> PTT-Lite.

papers.title: Distilling Large Language Models for Network Active Queue Management
papers.arxiv_note: v1 Jan 2025; v2 (Mar 2025) was WITHDRAWN; v3 Sep 2025 is the valid version
papers.COMPRESSION_MECHANISM_CORRECTION: DOES NOT PERFORM KNOWLEDGE DISTILLATION. Verified by me in the full text: there is no teacher-student KD anywhere in the paper. The mechanism is LoRA (rank r=128) + a data-driven offline reinforcement-learning adaptation pipeline. 'Distillation' is used loosely to mean transferring knowledge from existing AQM algorithms into an LLM. The '99% parameter reduction' is a reduction in TRAINABLE parameters (7B -> 70M) and does NOT reduce inference cost - the 7B weights remain at serving time. The authors themselves state in the conclusion that 'further refinement via pruning, quantization, and distillation toward small-language-model-based AQM can enhance scalability and resource efficiency' - i.e. real compression is FUTURE WORK. DO NOT CITE AS COMPRESSION OR KD EVIDENCE.
papers.base_model: Llama2-7B (primary), OPT-1.3B, GPT-2 (125M), T5-LLM (220M)
papers.method: LoRA rank r=128 + data-driven reinforcement learning; improved state encoder mapping network metrics to token embeddings (4096-dim for Llama2); extended LLM head giving single-inference congestion decisions (enqueue/drop/ECN-mark). NO KD, NO pruning, NO quantization.
papers.dataset_name: L4S (RFC 9330) active queue management with ECN marking (RFC 9331) + periodic packet dropping; FreeBSD-14 open-source implementation; DCTCP and UDP Prague
papers.dataset_size: pre-collected traces from existing AQM algorithms; size NOT REPORTED
papers.gpu_hardware: 2 x NVIDIA A40 (48 GB). VRAM: Llama2 23.91 GB, OPT 7 GB, GPT-2 3.6 GB, T5-LLM 2.32 GB.
papers.training_time: >20 hours for Llama2-7B vs sub-hour for OPT/GPT-2/T5
papers.inference_latency: Un-adapted Llama2-7B 0.200 s per answer; LoRA-adapted: Llama2 0.0391 s, OPT 0.0395 s, GPT-2 0.0414 s, T5-LLM 0.0411 s. ~80% inference-time reduction, ~5x speedup. LoRA gives -64% GPU memory and -15.1% training time.
papers.model_size_after_compression: UNCHANGED (7B). '99% reduction' refers to trainable parameters only.
papers.main_results: Llama2-7B 97.56% accuracy vs 82-83% plateau for OPT, GPT-2 and T5-LLM. LoRA reduces trainable params 7B -> ~70M (1%) while maintaining accuracy. Reduced delay variability and enhanced bandwidth utilisation across DCTCP and UDP Prague.
baselines: classical AQM: RED, CoDel, PIE, CAKE
papers.main_limitation: NO COMPRESSION PERFORMED. 39 ms latency far above packet-processing budgets (sub-millisecond is future work). >20 h training for a marginal accuracy gain over much smaller models (97.56% vs 82-83%) is a poor cost/benefit trade the paper does not analyse.

key_gaps_identified: STRUCTURAL EVIDENCE GAP: no paper retrieved reports a billion-parameter LLM teacher compressed into a network-domain SLM with full, reproducible compression hyperparameters. Well-documented compressions (MERLOT, Pruned Traffic Trees, OB-IDS, NetKD) all operate on GPT-2-base / BERT-base / GAT models at <=120M parameters. Papers that DO compress genuine LLMs (KGLlama-KD #20, MTNTD-SLM #24, SPARTA #54) each withhold a critical piece - temperature/alpha, teacher/student parameter counts, training hardware, or network-task evaluation. This is the single most promising gap for a PhD contribution.
No paper found that plots network-decision quality against model size or compression ratio. All size/compression trade-offs use NLP proxy metrics.

No paper found applying weight/neuron/layer/attention-head pruning to a fully-reported LLM for network management with a pruning ablation on a network task. SPARTA is the only billion-param pruning but validates on Wikitext2.
Inference latency is the field's biggest reporting gap, and the most-cited telecom-LLM latency number (300-500 ms) comes from a NON-PEER-REVIEWED vendor blog (TSLAM-8B).
The field has benchmarks for what telecom LLMs KNOW (TeleQnA, Tele-Eval, TelBench, TeleMath, GSMA leaderboard) but almost none for what they DO to a network.
'Telco-LLM', 'TelecomLLM' and 'LLaMA-Telecom' do not exist as papers - verified independently twice via Crossref and arXiv.

trafficllm_disambiguation.warning: There are THREE distinct things called TrafficLLM - do not conflate them.

variants.a: The one MERLOT benchmarks against (7B Llama2) is NOT a paper - MERLOT's reference [8] is the GitHub repo https://github.com/ZGC-LLM-Safety/TrafficLLM (no venue, no DOI).

variants.b: That repo's actual paper: Tianyu Cui, Xinjie Lin, Sijia Li, et al., 'TrafficLLM: Enhancing Large Language Models for Network Traffic Analysis with Generic Traffic Representation,' PREPRINT arXiv:2504.04222 (v1 5 Apr 2025). 10 scenarios / 229 traffic types, F1 0.9875 (detection) / 0.9483 (generation). Compression: NO pruning/quantization/distillation - uses EA-PEFT + traffic-domain tokenization. No peer-reviewed venue DOI found.

variants.c: A different paper: Ginige, Silva, Dahanayaka, Seneviratne, 'TrafficLLM: LLMs for improved open-set encrypted traffic analysis,' Computer Networks 2026, DOI 10.1016/j.comnet.2025.111847 - open-set encrypted traffic, no compression found.

variants.d: Also: Chengming Hu et al., 'Self-Refined Generative Foundation Models for Wireless Traffic Prediction' (the other 'TrafficLLM'), IEEE TVT, DOI 10.1109/TVT.2025.3637245 - wireless traffic PREDICTION, no compression.

terminology_drift_warning: Count mechanisms, not titles. Two papers whose titles/framing imply knowledge distillation contain NO classical teacher-student KD: AQM-LLM (#17) is LoRA r=128 + offline RL (its '99% reduction' is TRAINABLE parameters, 7B->70M, which does not reduce serving cost), and Cost-Efficient KD Student Placement (#23) is a placement optimisation problem. HiPELog (#55) has the same LoRA framing issue. A title-keyword survey will substantially over-count compression evidence.
